questions.question: What was the new motto of Lokpal of India adopted by the full bench of Lokpal in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Empower Citizens, Expose Corruption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The new motto of the **Lokpal of India**, adopted by the full bench in **June 2025**, is "**Empower Citizens, Expose Corruption**."
 
• This motto reflects the Lokpal's commitment to **strengthening public participation** in governance and ensuring **transparency and accountability** in the fight against corruption.
 
• The motto emphasizes the dual role of the Lokpal: **empowering ordinary citizens** by addressing their grievances and **exposing corrupt practices** in public offices.
 
• The adoption of this motto aligns with the Lokpal's broader objective under the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**, which aims to combat corruption among public functionaries.
 
• By adopting this motto, the Lokpal aims to establish itself as a **citizen-centric institution**, encouraging whistleblowing and ensuring justice for victims of corruption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:**

 
 
• The **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act** was enacted in **2013** to establish the Lokpal at the central level and Lokayuktas at the state level for investigating cases of corruption against public servants.
 
• The Lokpal consists of a **chairperson** and up to **eight members**, half of whom must be judicial members and at least 50% from SC/ST/OBC, minorities, or women.
 
• The jurisdiction of the Lokpal covers the **Prime Minister (with specific safeguards), ministers, Members of Parliament, and group A, B, C, and D officers and officials** of the central government.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal is mandated to ensure **effective action against corruption** in public offices, thereby fostering **good governance**.
 
• The institution works towards **strengthening accountability** mechanisms and addressing citizens' grievances related to corruption.
 
 
 
• **Features of the Motto:**
 
 
• "**Empower Citizens**": This part of the motto focuses on enabling citizens to actively participate in governance and hold public officials accountable.
 
• "**Expose Corruption**": This emphasizes the Lokpal's role in uncovering and addressing corrupt practices, ensuring transparency and fairness in administrative processes.
 
 
 
• **Other Anti-Corruption Mechanisms in India:**
 
 
• **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):** Established to address corruption in central government organizations.
 
• **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI):** Investigates high-profile corruption cases and economic offenses.
 
• **Whistleblowers Protection Act, 2014:** Provides a mechanism to protect individuals who expose corruption or misuse of power by public servants.

questions.question: Which of the following departments released the 2025 Economic Survey of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Economic Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department of Economic Affairs** is a part of the **Ministry of Finance**, Government of India, and is primarily responsible for the preparation and release of the **Economic Survey of India**, including the **2025 edition**.
 
• The **Economic Survey** provides a detailed analysis of the country’s economic progress, challenges, and outlook for the coming financial year, serving as a precursor to the Union Budget.
 
• The Survey is typically released a day before the presentation of the Union Budget in **Parliament**. It is a crucial document for policymakers, economists, and researchers.
 
• The Department of Economic Affairs works closely with the **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)** to compile and prepare this document. The CEA plays a pivotal role in shaping its content and focus.
 
• The Survey addresses various aspects, such as **economic growth rates, fiscal policy, monetary policy, inflation trends, external sector performance, and employment statistics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Survey of India:**

 
 
• The **Economic Survey** is an annual document that reviews the performance of the Indian economy over the past year and presents policy recommendations for the upcoming year.
 
• The first Economic Survey of India was published in **1950-51** and was initially included in the Union Budget documents. It became a standalone document from **1964**.
 
• It is regarded as the government’s flagship economic report and is prepared under the guidance of the **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)**.
 
• The Survey is divided into two volumes: **Volume I** focuses on conceptual and analytical issues, while **Volume II** provides detailed statistical data and sectoral analysis.
 
 
 
• **Department of Economic Affairs (DEA):**
 
 
• The DEA is one of the five departments under the **Ministry of Finance**. It is responsible for handling the economic policy framework and financial regulations in India.
 
• Its functions include managing the **country’s external debt, currency exchange policies, and financial market regulations**.
 
• The department oversees the preparation of crucial financial documents, such as the **Union Budget, Economic Survey, and various fiscal reports**.
 
• It also collaborates with international organizations like the **IMF, World Bank, and Asian Development Bank** on financial and economic matters.
 
 
 
• **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA):**
 
 
• The CEA is the principal advisor to the government on economic matters and plays a vital role in preparing the **Economic Survey**.
 
• The position is typically held by an eminent economist with expertise in macroeconomic policy and research.
 
• The CEA provides inputs on issues such as **GDP growth, inflation, fiscal deficit, and structural reforms**.
 
• The tenure of the CEA is generally for **three years**, and the individual reports directly to the **Finance Minister**.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget vs. Economic Survey:**
 
 
• The **Union Budget** is a financial statement that outlines the government’s revenue and expenditure for the upcoming fiscal year. It is presented in **February** each year.
 
• The **Economic Survey**, on the other hand, is a review of the economy’s performance in the past year and includes policy suggestions to address current challenges.
 
• While the Budget is focused on fiscal planning, the Survey emphasizes broader economic trends and strategic recommendations.
 
• Both documents are critical for understanding the economic priorities and direction of the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Economic Survey** acts as a tool for initiating public discussions on economic policy and reform measures.
 
• It provides insights into topics like **climate change, digital economy, healthcare, education, and employment**.
 
• Recent editions have highlighted the importance of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat, green energy transition, and post-pandemic recovery**.
 
• India’s GDP growth rate projections and fiscal deficit targets are key features of the Survey that garner widespread attention.
 
• The Survey also includes innovative chapters, such as those on behavioral economics and data-driven governance, to address emerging challenges.

questions.question: On 29 April 2025, the Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) Pralhad Joshi launched the GHCI scheme to empower MSMEs and promote green hydrogen economy. What is the full form of GHCI?

options.text: Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India
Green Hydrogen Cultivation Scheme of India
Green Hydrogen Channel Scheme of India
Green Hydrogen Conservation Scheme of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI)** was launched by **Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy, Pralhad Joshi,** on **29 April 2025**.
 
• The aim of the scheme is to **empower MSMEs (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises)** and promote the **green hydrogen economy**, a crucial step toward achieving sustainability goals.
 
• The scheme focuses on the **certification of green hydrogen production** to ensure that it is produced using renewable energy sources, adhering to global standards for carbon neutrality.
 
• The GHCI will provide a framework for **monitoring, verifying, and certifying green hydrogen**, enabling India to establish itself as a reliable supplier of green hydrogen in the global market.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s commitment to achieving **net-zero emissions by 2070** and its **National Hydrogen Energy Mission**, announced in 2021.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Green Hydrogen:**

 
 
• **Green hydrogen** is produced through the process of **electrolysis** of water using renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, or hydropower.
 
• It is considered a **clean energy source** as it produces no carbon emissions, making it crucial for decarbonizing industries like steel, cement, and transportation.
 
• Global demand for green hydrogen is expected to **increase exponentially** as countries aim to meet their climate targets under the Paris Agreement.
 
 
 
• **Role of MSMEs in the Green Hydrogen Economy:**
 
 
• MSMEs play a significant role in manufacturing and innovation within the green hydrogen supply chain.
 
• The GHCI scheme is expected to provide these enterprises with **financial incentives, technical support, and market access** to adopt green hydrogen technologies.
 
 
 
• **National Hydrogen Energy Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in **2021**, this mission focuses on the production and export of green hydrogen to position India as a global leader in clean energy.
 
• The mission seeks to reduce India’s dependence on fossil fuels and **achieve energy self-reliance**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Germany, Japan, and Australia** are investing heavily in green hydrogen as a part of their energy transition strategies.
 
• The certification process under GHCI will align India’s green hydrogen production with **international standards**, enhancing its export potential.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Green Hydrogen:**

 
 
• Green hydrogen is expected to replace fossil fuels in energy-intensive sectors and contribute to reducing **global greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• It is also a key component of India's strategy to become a **global leader in renewable energy**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Adopting Green Hydrogen:**
 
 
• The production of green hydrogen is currently **cost-intensive** due to the high costs of renewable energy and electrolyzers.
 
• GHCI aims to address these challenges by fostering innovation and scaling up production technologies to reduce costs.

questions.question: In June 2025, which of the following announced to introduce 'Validated UPI Handles' effective from 1 October 2025 for secured payments by investors to enhance investor protection and combat fraud?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** announced the introduction of **'Validated UPI Handles'** in **June 2025**, effective from **1 October 2025**, aiming to ensure **secured payments** by investors.
 
• The initiative is designed to **enhance investor protection** and combat fraudulent practices, marking a significant step toward improving transaction security in the financial markets.
 
• SEBI is the **regulatory authority** for the securities and capital markets in India, established under the **Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992**.
 
• The 'Validated UPI Handles' mechanism facilitates **two-factor authentication**, ensuring that payments are routed securely between investors and intermediaries.
 
• This move aligns with SEBI's broader efforts to promote transparency and safeguard the interests of retail investors in the Indian financial ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):**

 
 
• SEBI was established in **1992** to regulate the securities market in India and protect investors' interests.
 
• Its headquarters are located in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
 
• SEBI's primary functions include **regulating stock exchanges**, mutual funds, and brokers, and ensuring the orderly development of the securities market.
 
• It is empowered to investigate and take actions against fraudulent activities under the **Securities Contract Regulation Act, 1956** and the SEBI Act, 1992.
 
 
 
• **Unified Payments Interface (UPI):**
 
 
• UPI is a **real-time payment system** developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (**NPCI**) in **2016**.
 
• It allows instant money transfers between bank accounts using mobile devices, simplifying transactions for individuals and businesses.
 
• UPI has gained immense popularity due to its **ease of use**, **low transaction costs**, and robust security features.
 
• SEBI's initiative to validate UPI handles ensures that they are securely linked to investors' accounts to prevent fraudulent transactions.
 
 
 
• **Investor Protection Measures by SEBI:**
 
 
• SEBI has introduced multiple frameworks to safeguard retail investors, including **disclosures by mutual funds**, **strengthened KYC norms**, and **risk management systems**.
 
• It mandates brokers and intermediaries to implement secure payment mechanisms to protect investors' funds.
 
• Investor education programs are regularly conducted to spread awareness regarding safe investment practices.
 
 
 
• **Fraud Mitigation in Financial Transactions:**
 
 
• Fraudulent activities in the financial markets often stem from **unauthorized access** to payment gateways or investor accounts.
 
• SEBI's validation of UPI handles ensures that only legitimate and authenticated transactions occur, reducing the risk of fraud.
 
• Such mechanisms are essential for building investor confidence and fostering sustainable growth in the Indian securities market.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Life Insurance Corporation (LIC):**

 
 
• LIC is a government-owned insurance corporation established in **1956** under the **LIC Act**.
 
• It primarily provides life insurance policies and investment opportunities for individuals.
 
• While LIC plays a significant role in India's financial sector, it does not regulate securities or UPI transactions.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• RBI is India's central banking institution responsible for **monetary policy**, **currency issuance**, and financial stability.
 
• Although RBI oversees payment systems like UPI, SEBI governs securities market transactions, making it the authority behind this announcement.
 
 
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI):**
 
 
• SBI is India's largest public sector bank, providing banking and financial services to individuals and businesses.
 
• While SBI facilitates UPI transactions, it does not have regulatory powers over securities markets.

questions.question: What is the name of the first private-sector reinsurer to be licensed under the new framework of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Valueattics Reinsurance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Valueattics Reinsurance** became the first private-sector reinsurer to be licensed under the **new framework of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in **March 2025**.
 
• The **IRDAI** introduced the new framework to encourage private participation in the reinsurance sector, thereby enhancing competition and efficiency in the Indian insurance market.
 
• Reinsurance involves the transfer of portions of risk portfolios from primary insurers to reinsurers, ensuring stability and reducing the financial burden on insurance companies.
 
• The licensing of private reinsurers like **Valueattics Reinsurance** aligns with the government's objective to attract global investments and expertise into India's insurance sector.
 
• This initiative also aims to strengthen the domestic insurance market, making it more robust and capable of handling large-scale risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reinsurance:**

 
 
• Reinsurance is a financial arrangement where an insurance company transfers part of its risk to another company (reinsurer) to mitigate potential losses.
 
• It allows insurers to underwrite policies with higher limits while maintaining financial stability.
 
• Reinsurance can be categorized into two types: **Proportional Reinsurance** and **Non-Proportional Reinsurance**.
 
• Examples of global reinsurers include **Munich Re**, **Swiss Re**, and **Hannover Re**.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**
 
 
• Established in **2000**, IRDAI is the apex regulatory authority for the insurance and reinsurance sectors in India.
 
• It ensures the orderly growth of the insurance industry and protects policyholders' interests.
 
• IRDAI is headquartered in **Hyderabad**, Telangana.
 
• It also promotes innovation in insurance products and fosters fair competition among insurers.
 
 
 
• **Private Participation in Reinsurance:**
 
 
• The Indian government has opened up the reinsurance market to private and foreign companies to increase competition and efficiency.
 
• This move allows Indian insurers to access global expertise and innovative risk management solutions.
 
• It also facilitates better pricing of insurance products and improved claims settlement processes.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Licensing Private Reinsurers:**
 
 
• Private reinsurers bring additional capital to the insurance market, supporting its growth.
 
• They provide specialized risk management solutions tailored to specific needs.
 
• This development fosters a competitive environment, benefiting policyholders with better products and services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Reinsurance Market:**

 
 
• Reinsurance is a key component of the global financial system, with major markets in **Europe**, **North America**, and **Asia**.
 
• India's growing insurance market presents an opportunity for global reinsurers to expand their footprint.
 
 
 
• **IRDAI's Role in Promoting Reinsurance:**
 
 
• IRDAI has implemented policies to ease entry barriers for private and foreign reinsurers.
 
• It ensures a level playing field by regulating the operations of reinsurers in India.

• Modi has a significant presence on social media platforms such as **Twitter, Facebook**, and **Instagram**, showcasing his global outreach strategy.

• It has attracted several political figures and influencers globally, particularly from right-wing or conservative ideologies.
 
• Truth Social operates as an alternative to mainstream platforms like **Twitter** and **Facebook**.
 
 
 
• **Global Digital Diplomacy:**
 
 
• Many global leaders, including **Narendra Modi**, use digital platforms for diplomacy and outreach, helping them connect with citizens and international audiences.
 
• Digital diplomacy includes the use of social media channels to address global issues, foster international relations, and promote national interests.
 
• Platforms like **Twitter** and **Truth Social** have become critical tools for leaders to communicate directly with people worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Donald Trump:**
 
 
• Donald Trump served as the **45th President of the United States** from **2017 to 2021**.
 
• He launched Truth Social as a part of his media and technology group to counter censorship and promote free speech.
 
• Trump has been a prominent user of social media, often using platforms to directly communicate with the public.
 
• His initiatives like Truth Social aim to create platforms that align with his political and ideological goals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Social media platforms have become vital tools for political leaders to engage with their constituencies and global audiences.
 
• Platforms like **Truth Social** and **Twitter** allow leaders to share their viewpoints, policies, and achievements directly.
 
• Such platforms also play a significant role in shaping public opinion and fostering international communication.
 
• Leaders joining new platforms often signify shifts in diplomatic or political strategies to reach specific audiences.
 
 
 
• **Digital Outreach in Politics:**
 
 
• Digital outreach is increasingly critical in politics, enabling direct interaction between leaders and citizens.
 
• It helps leaders bypass traditional media channels and communicate their messages unfiltered.
 
• Such initiatives are vital for building transparency and fostering public trust.

questions.question: Who did Jannik Sinner defeat in the final of the Australian Open 2025?

__
 
• **Jannik Sinner**, an Italian professional tennis player, defeated **Alexander Zverev** in the final of the **Australian Open 2025** to claim his maiden Grand Slam title.

questions.question: In 2025, in which country was the Yala Glacier declared 'dead' due to the effects of climate change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Yala Glacier**, located in the **Langtang region of Nepal**, was officially declared "dead" in **2025** due to the severe impact of **climate change**.
 
• A glacier is considered "dead" when it no longer exhibits any signs of movement or replenishment from snowfall, effectively ceasing to function as a glacier.
 
• The declaration of the Yala Glacier's demise highlights the **accelerated melting of glaciers** in the Himalayan region, which is attributed to **rising global temperatures** caused by greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The Yala Glacier has been a critical source of **freshwater** for local communities and ecosystems, and its disappearance threatens water security in the region.
 
• This event underscores the urgent need for **international efforts** to combat climate change, particularly in vulnerable regions like the Himalayas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Yala Glacier:**

 
 
• The Yala Glacier is located in the **Langtang National Park**, approximately 28 kilometers north of Kathmandu, Nepal.
 
• It is situated at an altitude of around **5,000 meters** and has been a key site for **glaciological studies** for decades.
 
• The glacier has been retreating rapidly over the past few decades due to **global warming** and changes in precipitation patterns.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Glacier Melting in the Himalayas:**
 
 
• The Himalayan glaciers are often referred to as the **"Third Pole"** due to their vast ice reserves, which are crucial for water supply in Asia.
 
• Glacier melting leads to the **loss of freshwater resources**, affecting millions of people dependent on rivers originating from these glaciers, such as the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus.
 
• It also increases the risk of **glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs)**, which can cause catastrophic damage to downstream areas.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Glacier Retreat:**
 
 
• **Global Warming:** Rising global temperatures due to greenhouse gas emissions are the primary cause of glacier retreat worldwide.
 
• **Black Carbon:** Deposition of soot and black carbon on glacier surfaces accelerates melting by reducing the glacier's **albedo** (reflectivity).
 
• **Changes in Precipitation:** Altered monsoon patterns and reduced snowfall contribute to the shrinkage of glaciers in the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Global Efforts to Combat Climate Change:**
 
 
• The **Paris Agreement**, adopted in 2015, aims to limit global warming to **below 2°C** compared to pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.
 
• Organizations like the **International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD)** are working to address the impacts of climate change in the Himalayan region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Himalayan Glaciers at Risk:**

 
 
• The **Gangotri Glacier** in India, which feeds the Ganges River, has also been retreating rapidly over the years.
 
• The **Imja Glacier** in Nepal has formed a glacial lake, increasing the risk of GLOFs.
 
 
 
• **Role of Local Communities:**
 
 
• Local communities in the Himalayas are adopting **sustainable practices** to mitigate the impacts of glacier retreat.
 
• Efforts include **water conservation**, afforestation, and promoting awareness about climate change.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Research:**
 
 
• Continuous monitoring of glaciers using **satellite imagery** and field studies is crucial for understanding the pace of glacial retreat.
 
• Research institutions worldwide are collaborating to study the impacts of climate change on the Himalayas.

questions.question: The Indus Water Treaty, which was suspended by India following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, was signed between India and Pakistan in _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**1960**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Indus Water Treaty** was signed between **India and Pakistan** in the year **1960**. It was brokered by the **World Bank**. • The treaty governs the **utilization of the waters of the Indus River and its tributaries**, which flow through both India and Pakistan. • Under the treaty, the waters of the eastern rivers—**Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi**—are allocated to India, while the waters of the western rivers—**Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab**—are allocated to Pakistan. • The treaty ensures that Pakistan receives about **80% of the water from the Indus river system**, while India retains the remaining portion. • The treaty is often cited as one of the most successful examples of **water-sharing agreements** in the world, even persisting through periods of conflict between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: How many positions did India drop in the 2025 Energy Transition Index compared to the previous year?

__
 
• The **Energy Transition Index (ETI)** is an annual ranking published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, assessing countries' energy systems' readiness for transition to sustainable energy sources.
 
• In the **2025 ETI**, **India dropped by 8 positions** compared to the previous year's ranking, reflecting challenges in its energy transition efforts.
 
• The ETI evaluates countries on three core dimensions: **energy security and access, environmental sustainability, and economic development and growth.**
 
• The significant drop in India's ranking could be attributed to factors such as **increasing reliance on fossil fuels**, **slow progress in renewable energy integration**, and **challenges in energy policy implementation.**
 
• India's efforts in renewable energy deployment, such as the **National Solar Mission** and commitments under the **Paris Agreement**, are notable. However, systemic challenges like **grid infrastructure, financial viability**, and **energy equity** have impacted its performance in the ETI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Energy Transition Index (ETI):**

 
 
• The ETI is developed by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** in collaboration with partners to track the progress of energy systems globally.
 
• It analyzes over **115 countries** based on their current energy system performance and their readiness for transition.
 
• The index is based on metrics like **energy affordability**, **sustainability**, **security**, and **accessibility**.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has set an ambitious target of achieving **500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030**.
 
• Programs like the **National Solar Mission** aim to install **100 GW of solar energy capacity** by 2022 (extended targets under COP26).
 
• India is also promoting the use of **wind energy**, with a target of achieving **60 GW capacity**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in India's Energy Transition:**
 
 
• India's energy sector is still **heavily reliant on coal**, which contributes to carbon emissions and impacts environmental sustainability.
 
• Financial challenges, such as **debts in the power distribution sector**, hinder infrastructure development for renewable energy.
 
• Integration of renewables into the **national grid** remains a technical and logistical challenge.
 
 
 
• **Global Energy Transition Trends:**
 
 
• Countries like **Sweden, Switzerland, and Finland** have consistently ranked high on the ETI due to their focus on renewable energy, efficient energy use, and environmental policies.
 
• Developing countries face challenges in energy transition due to limited access to **technology, financing**, and **policy frameworks.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
